The next morning, Corna woke before the others while the sky showed only a hint of dawn, and quietly roused Saule, Palo, and Alba. Myrt nodded to them as they left camp; he had relieved Mar'dy of his watch.  They walked a good distance, away from the Schrykes in the trees, and away from Masha who was sleeping quite close to Mar'dy. The Säen had not been able to speak confidently for too long, and much had happened that needed to be discussed.

Once out of earshot, it was clear to the others that Corna preferred their conversation to remain secret from the rest of their party, and she clarified they may share whatever was discussed with the other Säen, except Groom.

"Diospyra left camp last night and has yet to return. The moons were bright and I worry for her. Furthermore, I do not trust this Chlora. She has enough magic to take the wings from the Schrykes, while flying herself! I've never encountered such magic in a mortal being before, and I do not believe it was coincidence that she and Groom came upon us almost as soon as we left the sea." The others nodded in agreement.

"I agree she is different, but she has yet to be hostile." Palo added. "I worry more about the Schrykes, and I suggest we leave before they recover their flying capabilities. Mar'dy has disrupted the order of things in Dire Vents. Have you forgotten the night we met him, how he rushed back into the ocean so voraciously?" Palo smiled. They were all quite fond of the Lot'dy.

Alba disagreed, and the slight shake of her head caused the slender long leaves of her crown to quiver white in the light of the moons. "The Schrykes are our friends and Mar'dy is no mere rebel. He has been chosen by the Gods, twice! He has spoken to Tempest, and I believe Pome blessed him as well. We were meant to find him and we are perfectly capable of collecting and studying plants wherever his path may lead. Surely the Schrykes would not consider a sentient being, chosen by the Gods, disorderly? It would be very arrogant to assume to know the way of the Gods or why they blessed Mar'dy. He may have been born a slave but his spirit has always been free."

The others quietly agreed.

They looked to Saule who spoke, "The Schrykes are indeed our allies, but I believe they may also be that arrogant. God Phyra has appeared to them also, and given them their orders. If they believe Mar'dy must face judgement, we must convince them that, to disrupt the path of a *Godchosen* being is the action that would, in fact, be disorderly. Who knows what Tempest had in store for his creature? It is not for us to say, but I believe we must protect him, no matter what it takes. Allowing the death of Mar'dy or worse, re-enslavement by the Naga would certainly displease Pome. Imprisoning someone with such spirit is wrong, like putting a bird in a cage and preventing it from flight."

"And Diospyra?" Corna asked the group. They thought for a moment.

Alba spoke first, "We do not know the way of her kind. She came to Mar'dy in a time of great need and led us to him. We have helped her understand who she was, perhaps her path takes her elsewhere, to some other being who needs her."

"Or," Palo added, "she may be back before we break camp. She has wandered away before. And, while it warms my heart to see Quircus again, I do not think we should prevent him from leaving with Masha, if that it what they desire."

Corna made a dismissive sound and looked to Saule, "I do not think she plans on leaving Mar'dy for a moment. Do not forget the vial of poison he carries around his neck. The vial that simply appeared in our camp the night we met him? We may not know exactly what it is, but that does not mean others do not. I believe this Chlora creature wants the vial."

This thought disturbed the others and they were silent again for a moment.

"We will go to the Tree of Life where the Chlora live and find out if this Masha creature can be trusted. We will send two Säen back to the Forest of Brotherhood to deliver our findings, and the rest of us will continue with Mar'dy wherever his path may lead. Maybe the Chlora will provide us with counsel. In the meantime, we must prevent Mar'dy from being taken by the Schrykes or seduced into giving away the vial of poison, while subtly suggesting to Groom that he and his companion should find their own path. And now let us wake the others and begin the day. We are close to the Tree of Life and I am eager for society."
